Thirty-nine comments

Bunker Hill

This is a pretty common tune that has come in & out of favor. Although it seems like a new new tune it is in fact quite an old tune. No one really knows how it came to be known as “Bunker Hill” most likely it is a reference to the battle. This tune is a favorite with a lot of the old time ceili bands, but was sometimes played very differently. I think the reason for this was that certain melodeons & two row boxes had no C natural. Which is a a huge part of the tune.

Brad

↳ Posted by jmeme on March 21st, 2024.

Re: Bunker Hill

I’m pretty sure that what Dermot Byrne is doing is playing the tune using B/C fingering on a C#/D accordion. ‘Master Seamus’, which precedes it, was written (by Charlie Lennon) in G, but Dermot plays that in A, so it would figure that he’s playing ‘Bunker Hill’ (which is usually in D) in B using B/C fingering for the key of A, but the C#/D accordion places it in B. Not that I’m suggesting that Dermot Byrne wouldn’t be capable of playing the tunes in A and B on a B/C box - because if anyone can, Dermot can!

↳ Posted by nicyffidil on September 15th, 2024.

Re: Bunker Hill

I’m pretty sure he plays that set on the C#/D. I transcribed the whole album note for note, and there’s something about that first tune that suggests A fingerings on C#/D.

Here’s ”Bunker Hill” on video (possibly the lowest quality on the entire youtube, but still …):
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5XR1bdVr8gw

By the way, ”B/C fingering” doesn’t really make sense since no B/C player would play it in Amix either.

For what it’s worth - Bmix is my ”home key” for this tune (on C#/D). It’s the first version I heard, and to this day, I don’t think I have it on any other recording in the original key of Dmix. For me, the journey was reversed as I had to (re-)learn it in Dmix.

↳ Posted by jeff_lindqvist on September 15th, 2024.

Re: Bunker Hill

Sorry, I didn’t make a very good job of explaining what I meant. G fingering on B/C is the same as A fingering on C#/D. And A mix fingering on B/C is the same as B mix in C#/D. Like Mairtín O’Connor, Dermot Byrne is equally adept at playing on both systems. I originally learnt the tunes on my B/C Hohner Black Dot. But if I play them using the same fingering on my C#/D Paolo Soprani they are in the same pitch as on the CD recording.
But you may be right…

↳ Posted by nicyffidil on September 18th, 2024.

↳ Posted by nicyffidil on September 18th, 2024.

Re: Bunker Hill

I have a few recordings of box players having at this tune, but the only commercial release is a late 60s one from James Keane. It’s on the first Paddy O‘Brien Tune Collection, and I also have a recording of the older P O’B going at it.

All these musicians play it in the usual Dmix, but these days you hear musicians play tunes in all kinds of nutty keys, I’m sure they could play it Amix, low or high.

↳ Posted by What's the name of this tune? on September 18th, 2024.

Re: Bunker Hill

”Why wouldn’t B/C players play in A mix, incidentally?”

Of course they do, but that (probably?) depends on the tune. There’s a load of tunes that are usually played in Amix, so those are likely kept in that key (unless they’re played a step lower - which is often the case).

Anyway, just saying that I think the video suggests C#/D. Even if Dermot Byrne has great control of the bellows, you can still see longer pull sequences, for instance.

Bunker Hill, X:13 - As played by Gussie Russel (1927-2004) on a whistle; 1974-01-19; Doonagore, Co. Clare.

This is from a recording I found on ITMA that I really enjoyed. I felt it deserved to be written up and shared.

I think it’s best to share the full ABC code of my setting here. It’s slightly different to the score posted above, mostly due to some feedback I’ve had from the site manager here (my version uses an unorthodox choice of time signature and length, and he’s already asked me not to do that in one other case - for jigs IIRC). Links to the recording are in the headers. I’ve added some comments to the “N:” headers.

X:1
T:Bunker Hill
T:As played by Gussie Russel (1927-2004) on a whistle; 1974-01-19; Doonagore, Co. Clare.
T:from ITMA | Selections from the McConnell Family Collection | October 2024
M:4/4
Q:1/4=110
L:1/16
D:ITMA | Selections from the McConnell Family Collection | October 2024
S:Gussie Russel
F: https://www.itma.ie/playlists/mcconnell-playlist-october24/?track=4
N:1. Just a rough attempt to transcribe how it was played the first
N:time round.
N:2. I’m using my own, admittedly idiosyncratic choice of time
N:signature and note length. The standard way has bars that are
N:half as long, using 4/4 with quavers. Here it’s 4/4 with
N:semiquavers. (I did wonder about using 4/2 with quavers. That
N:would be closer to the standard way but the four beats to a
N:bar would be slightly less clear IMO.)
